result.title: On the Depth Transfer of Neural Optimizers via L-Smoothness
result.summary: Scaling deep learning models efficiently requires predictable performance transfer across compute regimes. Establishing reliable hyperparameter transfer allows optimal training dynamics and structural choices to be discovered on low-cost proxy models, avoiding catastrophic failures during massive-scale training. Existing depth-transfer analyses are architecture-specific and heuristic: hyperparameter transfer is only justified through toy blocks, and both rely on infinite-depth dynamics, a specific initialization, and feature-learning criteria. Building on $L$-smoothness framework of Xu et al. (2026), we understand hyperparameter transfer as how do the Lipschitz and $L$-smoothness constants of the loss scale with the depth $K$? We show that inverse-depth residual branch scaling $α=Θ(1/K)$ is sufficient to make both constants depth-independent at fixed width, uniformly over the bounded parameter domain and for arbitrary $p\to q$ geometries. Because the bounds depend on each residual branch only through its Lipschitz and smoothness constants, the argument applies to general residual networks (including branches of block depth $\geq 2$ such as transformer and ResNet blocks) without assumptions on initialization or correlations between layer weights. Since the smoothness constant controls the curvature penalty in the descent inequality, our bounds motivate a learning-rate scale without an additional depth-dependent curvature correction for updates bounded in the prescribed norm. This provides a geometric explanation of inverse-depth residual scaling and its application to the operator-norm geometries associated with AdamW, Muon, and MOGA. Learning-rate sweeps on GPT-2 (depths 2--128) and CIFAR-100 ResNets (8--32 residual blocks) confirm that Muon and MOGA exhibit stable learning-rate transfer under these prescriptions, with a common optimal rate across a 64-fold increase in depth.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在 L-smoothness 框架下把超参深度迁移归结为损失的 Lipschitz 与光滑常数如何随深度 K 变化，证明逆深度残差分支缩放 α=Θ(1/K) 可使两常数与深度无关，并给出 AdamW、Muon、MOGA 的学习率设定，在 GPT-2（深度 2–128）与 CIFAR-100 ResNet 上验证学习率迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 逆深度残差缩放与「深度无关的光滑常数」这一结论，可能为 loop/latent 循环推理模型在迭代深度变化时的残差缩放与学习率选择提供训练线索，可供核查其是否适用于推理期状态更新的循环结构。
